plain.fix: short: For several hours; probably longer after eating it than smoking it, and longer after bigger doses. | how 3: The effects faded over several hours, probably more slowly when THC was eaten than when it was smoked or vaped. | how 4: People who use cannabis weekly or more were less affected than people who use it less often, but the study could not work out for how long.
plain.note: The authors say oral impairment 'may take longer' (oral model pseudo-R2 0.28). Regular use was compared with other, mostly occasional, use; only this review's model could not predict duration.

plain.fix: short: In sleep labs, cannabis taken by mouth did not reliably change sleep, compared with a dummy pill or with sleep before treatment. | how 1: Six studies compared cannabis medicines swallowed by mouth with a dummy pill (placebo) or with sleep before treatment. | how 4: Small early studies (1972 to 1982), mostly with high doses of THC, often found less dream sleep.
plain.note: One pooled study (Farabi 2014) was uncontrolled pre-post. Pooled results were null but single studies varied (Discussion: no consistent effects). Five of eight early administration studies found less REM; doses 'mostly' high.

plain.fix: how 3: The pooled data came from the first week after stopping, so this review cannot say how long the changes last.
plain.note: Days 1-3 and 4-6 describe the data taken for meta-analysis (3.1.5), not how long the studies followed people; the paper gives no duration.

plain.fix: but: One small fair test and four weaker studies, mostly at moderate to high risk of bias. | how 4: Other studies disagreed; in one, more people given the cream than not given it were admitted to hospital, a difference that could be chance.
plain.note: The retrospective studies ranged from low to high risk of bias (p. 498). Yusuf's 8 v 1 admissions was a non-significant trend, with no difference in admission rates.

plain.fix: short: In two small studies, haloperidol eased sickness more than a usual anti-sickness medicine, and people given haloperidol or droperidol went home sooner than people given other care.
plain.note: The comparison groups were missing: haloperidol v ondansetron (trial), droperidol v no droperidol (chart review). The droperidol review reported length of stay and antiemetic use, not symptom scores.
